record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: For the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations for a polytropic gas, is the Cauchy problem globally well posed in time for entropy weak solutions with large initial data in the space BV of functions of bounded total variation? In particular, can one obtain global existence, uniqueness, and physically meaningful entropy admissibility for large-BV data in the natural shock-wave setting?

evidence.quote: Global (in time) well-posedness of entropy weak solutions to the Cauchy problems of the one-dimensional Euler equations for polytropic gas dynamics in the space of functions with bounded total variations (which is BV space).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations for a polytropic ideal gas, written for the conserved variables (density ρ>0, momentum ρu, total energy E) on ℝ×(0,∞):

  ∂_t ρ + ∂_x(ρu) = 0,
  ∂_t(ρu) + ∂_x(ρu² + p) = 0,
  ∂_t E + ∂_x((E+p)u) = 0,

with E = ρe + ½ρu², pressure law p = (γ−1)ρe for some adiabatic constant γ>1, and specific internal energy e>0. An entropy weak solution is a bounded measurable solution of the system in the distributional sense that, in addition, satisfies the entropy inequality

  ∂_t(ρS(η)) + ∂_x(ρuS(η)) ≤ 0

for every convex entropy pair associated with the system (equivalently, the Lax/physical entropy admissibility condition at shocks).

Let BV(ℝ) denote the space of functions of bounded total variation on the real line. Given Cauchy data (ρ_0, u_0, e_0) ∈ BV(ℝ) with ρ_0, e_0 bounded away from 0 but with no smallness restriction on the total variation (large-BV data), determine whether the Cauchy problem admits, for all times t∈[0,∞), a globally defined entropy weak solution, and whether such a solution is unique within a natural class of admissible BV solutions. In other words: establish (or disprove) global existence, uniqueness, and entropy admissibility of entropy weak solutions in BV for arbitrarily large BV initial data.
artifact.status_search_result: Global well-posedness of entropy weak solutions to the 1D compressible Euler equations for a polytropic gas with large BV initial data is widely cited as an outstanding open problem. Glimm's theorem and subsequent work (Bressan, Liu, Yang, etc.) establish global existence and uniqueness only for small-BV data. Recent advances (e.g., Bressan–De Lellis and others) treat related issues, and analogous large-BV results have been obtained for the viscous 1D Navier–Stokes system, but the inviscid large-BV case for polytropic Euler remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Global Solutions of the One-Dimensional Compressible Euler Equations with Nonlocal Interactions via the Inviscid Limit
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses global solutions for 1D compressible Euler; large-BV well-posedness for polytropic Euler is treated as a long-standing open question, with results restricted to small total variation or special structures.
status_evidence.claim: Global well-posedness for large-BV data for the 1D polytropic Euler system has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Global well-posedness of the 1d compressible Navier-Stokes system with rough data
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes global well-posedness for the 1D compressible Navier–Stokes system with BV data, contrasting with the inviscid Euler case.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous BV results exist for viscous 1D Navier–Stokes but not for inviscid Euler with large BV data.
